base-cabinet: A kitchen-style base cabinet, sized to take a standard countertop: a drawer over a door, with a recessed toe kick. Concealed hinges and full-extension slides are on the hardware list.
bed-frame: A queen platform bed, no box spring needed: 2x10 rails on 4x4 legs, with slats on ledgers and a centre beam. Comes apart to move.
bookcase-doors: A tall oak-plywood bookcase with two open shelves up top and a cupboard below behind a pair of doors on concealed hinges.
bookshelf: A tall, open five-bay bookshelf cut from plywood. One of the simplest things to build that still looks like furniture.
coffee-table: A low coffee table with a plywood top and a display shelf underneath, on solid legs.
desk: A four-leg writing desk with aprons under the top and plenty of legroom below. Solid legs, plywood top.
desk-drawers: A plywood desk with a three-drawer pedestal on one side and a panel leg on the other. Soft-close slides and bar pulls.
dining-table: A dining table that seats six, with an oak-plywood top on solid oak legs and aprons, joined with pocket screws.
dresser: A three-drawer dresser with graduated drawers on soft-close slides and matching bar pulls. Plywood carcase with an overhanging top.
entry-bench: A bench for the hallway with a shoe shelf underneath, cut from pine boards you can buy at any lumberyard.
entry-shelf: A wall shelf for the hallway: a shelf on top and a rail of coat hooks below. It screws into two studs.
garage-shelving: Heavy-duty freestanding garage shelving: four plywood shelves on 2x4 frames between 4x4 posts. Built for bins and paint cans.
kitchen-cart: A rolling kitchen cart at counter height, with a lower shelf. Maple frame, plywood top, and locking casters so it stays put.
media-console: A low media console in walnut plywood: an open centre bay for the electronics between two cupboards with concealed hinges.
mobile-workbench: A big, sturdy workbench on locking casters, with a lower shelf. A 2x4 frame under a plywood top at a comfortable working height.
nightstand: A bedside table with one drawer on soft-close slides and an open shelf below. Birch plywood, with a bar pull.
picnic-table: The classic six-foot A-frame picnic table with attached benches, all from 2x lumber and bolted together.
planter-box: A small cedar planter box: five boards, a few screws, an afternoon.
raised-bed: An 8 × 3 ft raised garden bed in cedar 2x10s on 4x4 corner posts. No finish needed.
record-stand-dado: A 38" record stand with a door, a turntable platform and a shelf for the receiver. Shelves sit in dados cut into the sides, for builders with a router or dado stack.
record-stand: A simple record stand: an 18 mm birch box with a middle shelf, holding a row of LPs on each level.
sawhorse: A 2x4 sawhorse with a replaceable beam. Build two and you have a work surface anywhere.
shoe-rack: A three-tier shoe rack with slatted shelves, so wet shoes can dry. Pine boards and pocket screws.
side-table: A small side table with a plywood top and a lower shelf on solid pine legs.
step-stool: A sturdy step stool from a single pine 1x12 and a scrap of 1x4. A good first project.
tool-tote: An open tool tote with a dowel handle, to carry a set of hand tools around the shop or the house.
toy-chest: A plywood toy chest with a hinged lid, a soft-close lid stay so it can't slam on fingers, and a handle on each end.
wall-cabinet: A plywood wall cabinet with a pair of inset doors on concealed hinges and a middle shelf. Hangs on two studs.
workbench: A sturdy workbench with a plywood top on a 2x4 frame. The first thing many shops build.
workbench-drawers: A shop workbench with a doubled plywood top, two drawers under it and a full shelf below, on 4x4 legs.
picket-planter: A cedar planter from dog-eared fence pickets on a 2x2 frame: one of the cheapest weekend builds there is.
bench-planter: Two picket planters with a cedar deck-board seat between them: a garden bench with room to plant at each end.
birdhouse: A cedar birdhouse from a single 1x6, with a dog-eared gable, a lapped roof and a vent under the eaves.
